claim: The sterile-nu server gives DW Omega_s h^2 proportional to sin^2 2theta. At sin^2 2theta = 1e-12 it returns Omega_s h^2 = 0.003041 (20 keV), 0.00361 (22 keV), 0.005936 (29 keV), 0.01309 (45 keV) and 0.0004715 (7.1 keV). Linear scaling to f_s = Omega_s h^2/0.12 = 1 then gives sin^2 2theta(f_s=1) of about 3.95e-11, 3.32e-11, 2.02e-11, 9.17e-12 and 2.55e-10 respectively. At the 3.5 keV line point (7.1 keV, 7e-11) the tool gives Omega_s h^2 = 0.033, i.e. f_s = 0.275.

At the DW f_s = 1 mixing, the tool's X-ray check gives: 20 keV with sin^2 2theta = 3.95e-11 is EXCLUDED by NuSTAR M31 (Roach+ 2020); 29 keV (2.02e-11) and 45 keV (9.17e-12) are 'not excluded', but only because no tabulated limit lies within 30% in mass. Those two masses are uncovered by the tool, not shown to be allowed. The tool also does not return the numerical limit on sin^2 2theta, so f_s at the X-ray limit cannot be read directly from it.

A DW scan of 6400 points over m_s = 1-100 keV and sin^2 2theta = 1e-14 to 1e-6 gives 3092 overclosing points (Omega_s h^2 > 0.12) and 968 BBN-excluded points. BBN is weak for keV DW: the largest BBN-allowed mixing is 3.03e-8 at 26.2 keV and 1.5e-8 at 49.7 keV, about 3 orders of magnitude above the f_s = 1 line. BBN therefore does not constrain DW dark matter; only X-ray limits and Lyman-alpha do. The exclusion plot is Figure 25.

At the 3.5 keV line point (7.1 keV, sin^2 2theta = 7e-11), the DW fraction depends on the normalisation: f_s = 0.275 with the tool, 7e-11/7.88e-10 = 0.089 with the ALS conservative line, and 7e-11/3.02e-9 = 0.023 with Abazajian 2006. The headline DW production fraction is therefore uncertain by a factor of about 3 to 12. The tool is the most optimistic of the three (largest f_s), so its X-ray exclusion of f_s = 1 at 20 keV (f-002) only gets stronger under the published normalisations.
